newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New Swiss telecom provider starts service.
newsitem.headline: New Swiss telecom provider starts service.

text.p: A Swiss telecommunications venture by three major enterprises, including Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), will start offering broad band data services to business customers from November 1.
Newtelco AG, formed in February, said on Friday it would also offer the services to Internet providers.

It said lines carrying large amounts of data were the first step towards a full range of data, voice and multimedia services planned from the start of 1998, when Switzerland is to open its telecommunications market in step with the surrounding European Union.
Newtelco was formed by UBS, the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) and retail cooperative Migros, which dominates the Swiss department store market.

The consortium will base operations on a new and underused national net of fibre-optic cable owned by the SBB and now used solely by the railways. It will also utilise private networks run by UBS and Migros.
"This telecoms newcomer (Newtelco) can therefore offer broad band data services nearly everywhere in Switzerland," a statement said.
Newtelco said it was going ahead with data services despite not having yet found an experienced telecommunications partner to guide operations, a goal it had set back in February.
A spokesman said Newtelco was in negotiations with potential partners and felt it could ahead alone in starting data services.
Newtelco will not only be competing from 1998 with a partially-privatised Swiss Telecom, but also a consortium of Swiss power utilities formed in July and named DIAX.

Efforts to liberalise the Swiss telecommunications market have been under way for several years and a first step was taken in 1991 when Switzerland allowed private companies to offer some kinds of data transmission.

The Swiss parliament is expected to approve a full liberalisation during 1997 so the monopoly held by Swiss Telecom PTT over most voice transmission and the cellular phone network can be lifted at the same time as the EU liberalises its communications market on January 1, 1998.
